questionsNeedingReview.question: What are the construction characteristics of thee basic types of fuel tanks?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: The three types of tanks are rigid, bladder, and integral tank. The rigid tank is usually made of aluminum or stainless steel and is riveted and has welded seams to prevent leaks. Rigid tanks are removable. Some modern rigid tanks are made from composite materials. Bladder tanks are made from a reinforced flexible material. Bladder tanks are also removable. Bladder tanks are repairable by patching and other techniques in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Integral tanks are formed as part of the wing or part of the fuselage and is sealed with a fuel resistant two part sealant to prevent leaks. A integral tank is not removable as it is part of the main structure of the aircraft. They are repairable by draining, cleaning, and resealing. All fuel tanks regardless of their construction must have means for venting, have a sump located at the lowest point where water and sediment can collect and be drained out. Many tanks have baffles to prevent the rapid movement of fuel during flight maneuvers and scuppers to drain away any spilled fuel at fill port areas.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What is the purpose of a fuel jettison system and what are some characteristics of a typical fuel jettison system?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: If an aircraft's design landing weight is less than that of maximum take off weight, a situation could occur in which a landing is desired before sufficient fuel has burned off to lighten the aircraft to or below the acceptable landing weight. Fuel jettisoning systems are required in these aircraft so that the fuel can be jettisoned in flight to avoid structural damage caused by landing the aircraft when it is to heavy. Characteristics of a fuel jettison systems are, the rate of fuel jettisoning as well as the various attitudes, speeds, and configurations of the aircraft are taken into consideration. The fuel must discharge clear of any part of the aircraft. The discharge of the fuel must not affect the controllability of the aircraft. There must be enough redundancy so that the failure of a single component does not prevent the fuel from being jettisoned. Also, the process of jettisoning fuel must be able to be controlled by a valve and stopped if desired. The amount of fuel able to be jettisoned is also controlled.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Explain the purpose and operation of a gyroscopic instrument.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Most gyroscopic instruments are used for direction or attitude indication. They can be driven by air pressure, vacuum, or electricity since the spinning armature of a motor can act as a gyroscope. When rotating a gyroscope it maintains rigidity in space. That is, it will continue to rotate in the same plan of rotation no matter which way its mounting gimbals are moved. This is the basis of a directional gyro. The directional gyro, or DG is commonly relied upon more than the magnetic compass to indicate direction in an aircraft. The gyro spins in the vertical plane and stays aligned with the direction to which it is set. The instrument case and the aircraft move around the ridged gyro. This causes a vertical compass card geared to the rotor gimble to rotate. Typically, a small, fixed airplane in front of the moving card indicates the direction in degrees.

questionsNeedingReview.question: How does a pitot and static system operate?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: A pitot system captures air pressure as the aircraft moves forward through the air. Air travels through the pitot tube and the air pressure is converted to an airspeed indicator, and to the digital air date computer (if in use). The pressure is used to calculate and display airspeed. The static system is designed to sense ambient atmospheric pressure. Input air is either from static ports in the pitot tube, or from dedicated flush- mounted heated, static ports located on the side of the fuselage. The pressure is conveyed through a series of airtight tubes to the instruments that require the use of atmospheric pressure. This includes the air speed indicator, the variometer and the altimeter. On a modern more complex aircraft, the static system conveys ambient air pressure to a digital air data computer. In addition, the computer processes the ambient air pressure outputs for the auto-pilot system, the transponder, the flight management computers, IRS navigation units and more.

Licensed airframe and A&P technicians may perform this check. A test unit is used to check the system. It is attached to the static port end of the static system. Air pressure is then reduced by the test unit until it causes 1,000 feet to be indicated on the altimeter. This pressure is held for one minute. A reduction of altitude indication of more than 100 feet is not allowed. Systematic leak checking must be performed until the leak is located, repaired, and the system passes the check.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Briefly describe the vapor cycle of a vapor cycle air conditioning system.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: A vapor cycle air conditioning system is a closed system with refrigerant in it. It is used to transfer heat from inside the cabin to outside the cabin. Heat energy is moved from the cabin air into liquid refrigerant by blowing cabin air over a heat exchanger (evaporator) containing refrigerant. The vapor is then compressed, due to the additional energy, the vapor becomes very hot. The very hot vapor is then routed to different heat exchanger (condenser,) where the vapor turns to a liquid or (condenses.)Then the heat from the refrigerant is transferred to the outside. The cycle is than repeated (Vapor Cycle.) Components of the vapor cycle system are as follows: Evaporator, Compressor, condenser, receiver dryer, expansion valve. Be prepared to discuss the function of each component with the examiner.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Explain the two basic modes of cabin pressurization and name the single component that modulates to control the pressure of the air in the cabin during both modes of operation.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Two modes are isobaric mode and differential pressure mode. In isobaric mode, the pressurization system works to maintain a single pressure inside the cabin, known as cabin altitude, despite the altitude of the aircraft or the pressure of the ambient air outside the aircraft. In differential mode, the system controls the cabin pressure to maintain a constant pressure difference between the air inside the cabin and the air outside the aircraft regardless of altitude changes. The single device that opens and closes, or modulates to control air exiting the cabin, and thus, the air pressure in the cabin is the outflow valve.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What type of oxygen system is typically used on light, general aviation aircraft and what type(s) is used on transport category aircraft?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Many light aircraft do not have an oxygen system if the aircraft is not designed to fly at altitudes that require oxygen. Some small general aviation aircraft may have a portable oxygen bottle on board to be used by the crew when desired. A built in system may exist that uses approved containers of gaseous oxygen. Both are typically delivered through regulated, continuous flow systems where oxygen is supplied at a steady rate when the valve of the oxygen container is opened. However, electronic pulse demand oxygen delivery systems are currently available for general aviation aircraft. These type pulse oxygen system only delivers oxygen to the user when they inhale creating a demand- type system. Oxygen is carried on transport category aircraft for emergency purposes only. During normal operation the cabin pressure provides enough oxygen for the crew and passengers. Gaseous and solid oxygen are used in an emergencies when pressurization is lost. The gaseous oxygen is stored in remote, pressurized tanks and routed to the users thorough a system of tubes. Solid oxygen generators produce gaseous oxygen for use when ignited. Passengers receive the oxygen from either source through a continuous flow delivery system. Most crew oxygen is delivered via demand flow or pressure- demand flow type regulators.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Name some precautions when performing maintenance on aircraft oxygen systems.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Always keep clothing, hands, and tools clean, make sure there is no grease or oily residue around or near oxygen when servicing. A good maintenance practice is to have dedicated tools for servicing oxygen only. Never smoke or have an open flame within 50 feet of the work area when servicing oxygen. Always use protective plugs or caps when working with oxygen cylinders, system components or plumbing. Do not use any kind of adhesive tape. Oxygen cylinders should be stored in a designated, cool, ventilated area in the hanger away from petroleum products or heat sources. Fittings should be turned slowly to allow any residual pressure to dissipate. All oxygen lines should be marked and should have at least two inches of clearance from moving parts, electrical wiring, and all fluid lines. A pressure leak check must be performed each time the system is opened for maintenance. Do not use any lubricants, sealers, cleaners, etc., unless specifically approved for oxygen use.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What is the means of identification of commonly used communication and or navigation antennas?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: The shape and length of an antenna can sometimes be used to reason what type of antenna is under consideration. The orientation or polarization and location on the aircraft can also give clues. The three basic types of antennas are: the dipole, the Marconi, and the loop. Dipole antennas, often used for VOR frequencies, may have a “V” shape. They are commonly located at the empennage or mounted on the underside of the fuselage. The “V” shape indicates its horizontal polarization that makes the antennas good at receiving signals that are not coming head on. The Marconi antenna is simply a straight conductor. It uses the skin or on fabric aircraft, conductive material under the skin, to form a conductor of 2 wavelength of the signals it is designed to receive or transmit. The Marconi antenna is vertically polarized and creates a field that is omnidirectional. VHF communication radios can use this type of antenna. The conductor in a loop antenna forms a loop. Having a loop shape to receive radio signals significantly affects the field characteristics of the antenna. It is highly sensitive to the direction from which the signal is received. Loop antennas are used extensively in navigation such as for an ADF radio. Often the loop antennas are enclosed in a housing broad enough to conceal the entire antenna which is frequently mounted on the underside of the fuselage.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What are some common faults and trouble shooting techniques used on a fire detection system?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Intermittent alarms most often are caused by loose wires can often be found by moving the wires to recreate the fault. Alarms and warnings of a fire when there is no fire present can be located by disconnecting the sensors from the control unit. If the alarm stops when the sensor is disconnected, the problem is the sensor. if all sensors are disconnected and the alarm continues, the problem is likely the control unit. Kinks and sharp bends in a sensing element can cause a short inside the sensing element. The fault can be located by checking the element with an ohm- meter while tapping the suspected areas to produce the short. Failure to obtain an alarm when a detection system is tested is often caused by a defective test switch or control unit, lack of electric power, inoperative indicator lamp or an opening in a sensing element or connecting wire. Check for power to test the circuit and replace the lamp. The continuity of a sensing loop can be determined by opening the loop and measure the resistance. Replacement of the test switch or control unit may be required if no other faults are discovered. Occasionally moisture can cause a false alarm. This is detected in a sensor loop when disconnected from the control unit. Replacement of the sensor solves the problem.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What are some Hydraulic system maintenance precautions used to prevent contamination?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Only the correct, specified fluid must be used to service an aircraft hydraulic system. Keep all tools and work area clean. Use a proper container for capturing hydraulic fluid. Clean the fittings and area around them. Cap and plug all lines immediately after disconnecting. Before assembly, wash all parts in approved solvent. lubricate parts and seals before assembly. Replace all seals and gaskets with new. Only use seals and gaskets with the proper part number. Connect and torque all lines. Make sure hydraulic tools and equipment are clean and in good operating condition.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What are some common types and characteristics of hydraulic fluids, where are they used and how can they be identified?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: There are three types of hydraulic fluids: Mineral- based, Polyalaphaolefins, Phosphate esters. Mineral- based fluid is processed from from petroleum. It is dyed red and and has an odor similar to penetrating oil. The most common is MIL-H-5606. Mostly used in small aircraft where fire hazard is low. Polyalaphaolefins, oil is more fire resistant type of hydraulic oil, sometimes used in aircraft that normally use MIL-H- 5606. It is compatible with the same seals used for mineral based hydraulic systems. Phosphate ester-based (Skydrol) hydraulic fluid is used mostly in commercial transport category aircraft. It is dyed purple and fire resistant but not fire proof. Due to the difference in composition Phosphate ester-based and 5606 will not mix, and the seals used are also incompatible with the other. Do not try to mix hydraulic fluids, each hydraulic fluid is dyed a different color as to easily identify which hydraulic fluid it is. Always check the maintenance manual for the correct fluid to be used.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Name and describe five types of sheet metal defects.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: 1. Burnishing- a polishing caused by two surfaces sliding together with a hard or smooth surface, usually there is no removal of metal. 2. Crack- A physical separation of two adjacent portions of metal. Evidence of a crack, a thin line across the surface, a few thousands of an inch to completely through the metal caused by excessive stress. 3. Dent- Indentation of the metal surface produced by an object striking with force. The surface around the indentation is usually slightly upset. 4. Inclusion-Presence of foreign or extraneous material wholly with in a portion of the material. Inclusions are introduced during manufacturing process. 5. Score- deeper than a scratch, tear or break in the metal that results from contact under pressure. May show discoloration from temperature do to friction. Other defects are Brinelling, Burr, Corrosion, Cut, Erosion, Chattering, Galling, Gouge, Nick, Pitting, Scratch, Stain and Upsetting.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What actions are taken to install a rivet?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: Transferring and preparing original hole, drilling and driving rivets. Holes must be correctly located. Accomplish transfer of holes from a drilled part to another part by placing one part over the other using original holes as a guide. A scribe can also be used to transfer holes from the drilled part. Make sure to use the correct size drill bit for the the rivet being used. All burrs and chips must be removed. Make sure to use the proper size clecos to be sure all the holes line up perfectly. When riveting with a partner make sure to communicate using a code 1knock, 2Knocks, 3knocks and inspect the rivet shop head for proper width and height. Also check for looseness and proper installation.

questionsNeedingReview.question: What are some precautions when working with Magnesium, CRES and Titanium?
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: When working with corrosion resistant steel (CRES) a finish must be applied or it will cause corrosion to other metals when mated together. Also a lager bend radius must be selected to prevent cracking. Magnesium and titanium particles can easily ignite so work with these materials far away from any ignition source. If a fire does breakout use dry talc, calcium carbonate, sand and graphite to extinguish both magnesium and titanium fires. Do not use water, foam, carbon tetrachloride or carbon dioxide.

questionsNeedingReview.question: Describe the steps involved in a dye penetrant inspection.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: The surface is cleaned, and then penetrant is applied and allowed to dwell for a specified time. The penetrant is then removed with an emulsifier or cleaner. Once removed, the part is dried and then developer is applied. The results are then inspected and interpreted.

questionsNeedingReview.question: List the steps in a dye-penetrant inspection.
questionsNeedingReview.expectedAnswer: 1. Thoroughly clean the materials surface. 2. Apply the penetrant for the specified dwell time. 3. Remove the penetrant with water or emulsifying cleaner. 4. Dry the part. 5. Apply the developer. 6. Inspect the results.
